_notes: Single source of truth for CDR access control. Read by jobs/03_create_groups.py,
jobs/04_verify_rbac.py and jobs/05_fine_grained_controls.py. Do not edit grants or
policies directly in the notebooks.
Seven roles, the final provisioned set (2026-10-28 team decision), one per Unity Catalog
control that the PoC has to demonstrate:
cdr_admins                 all layers, full administration - SELECT + MODIFY, unmasked. The
unrestricted baseline every other role is compared to.
cdr_data_engineers         platform / pipeline engineering - read/write/build on all three
layers, unmasked where operationally required.
Engineering access without security administration.
cdr_data_scientist         ML / data science - schema SELECT on silver only, direct and
quasi identifiers masked. User-level separation:
no gold access, no security administration.
cdr_standard_researcher    column level   - schema grant on gold, identifiers arrive as NULL.
cdr_researcher_psychiatry  row level      - same grant and posture as the standard researcher,
but the row filter lets PSYCH rows through.
cdr_pharmacy_analyst       table level    - no schema SELECT at all; SELECT on the tables
carrying domain=pharmacy.
cdr_external_researcher    table level, narrow - approved diagnostic tables only, direct
identifiers masked per the final role matrix.
Row level needs a contrast to be visible: cdr_standard_researcher (level 1) and
cdr_researcher_psychiatry (level 2) hold identical privileges, so the only difference in a
query result is the row filter. That is the demonstration.
cdr_mortality_investigator was removed in the same decision. Consequence, accepted:
hl7_confidentiality = V_Very_Restricted data (deathtime) is now readable only by the
platform roles (cdr_admins, cdr_data_engineers); every research role receives NULL.
IMPORTANT: 03_create_groups never revokes, so any grant groups removed from this catalog
already hold in the metastore survives this edit. Revoke or drop them in the account
console, or the catalog says seven while the metastore still says more.
policy values: unmasked | masked | redacted
unmasked : original value
masked   : NULL
redacted : placeholder (REDACTED / -1), used where the PDF says Redacted
schemas: privileges granted at schema level (ALL domains roles)
domains: ALL, or the gold 'domain' tag values this role may read
rls: level 3 = global, 2 = standard rows + cohort, 1 = standard rows only
rls.id_anchored_filters: the same cohort rule anchored on a key instead of a service column,
for the gold tables that carry neither. Each filter body reads ONLY an rbac snapshot, never
a gold table: Unity Catalog rejects a filter that references another table carrying a filter
(UNSUPPORTED_NESTED_ROW_OR_COLUMN_ACCESS_POLICY) and takes the protected table offline. The
snapshots (hadm_service_map, subject_service_map, patient_service_map) are stale after a Gold
rebuild and are refreshed by re-running jobs/05; order details are anchored at patient level.
refreshed by re-running jobs/05. Function names carry the anchor type because a row filter
parameter has to match the column type: hadm_id is INT on nine gold facts and BIGINT on three.
patient_key is LONG and BIGINT is the resulting filter parameter type.
masking.masked_schemas: the schemas whose tagged columns carry enforced masks.
Gold and silver. Silver identifiers are masked because a role whose policy says
'masked' must not be able to read the raw identifier one schema down; the mask is
the second layer behind the schema grant, not a substitute for it.
masking.deferred_columns: per schema, columns that are classified but deliberately not
masked. Gold defers the join keys between facts; silver defers nothing.
masking.exempt_columns: per entry, the schema the exemption applies to.

masking._deferred_note: Per schema. In gold these are the join path between facts for researchers, so masking them would break joins for exactly the roles that are allowed to read the rows; the team decision on them is still outstanding. In silver nothing is deferred: they are read only through a schema grant, and a role whose policy says 'masked' must not see them raw.

exempt_columns.reason: Sex is required for cohort description and readmission/mortality analysis; on its own it cannot identify an individual in a de-identified extract.
Age banding is the primary confounder in every clinical analysis; MIMIC-IV already shifts dates and collapses 89+ to 91, so age alone is not identifying here.

masking._exempt_note: Still tagged phi_quasi_identifier (the classification is true) but deliberately NOT masked: these columns stay readable for every catalog role. This is an accepted residual re-identification risk, not an oversight. Reported as EXEMPT by 05 and as a note by 04.

cdr_admins.description: Schema-level control: platform administration with SELECT + MODIFY on bronze, silver and gold, unmasked. Also the identity the build pipelines run as

cdr_standard_researcher.description: Column-level control: granted the whole gold schema, so the only thing standing between this role and a raw identifier is the column mask

cdr_researcher_psychiatry.description: Row-level control: identical grants and column posture to cdr_standard_researcher, so the only difference in the result set is the row filter

cdr_pharmacy_analyst.description: Table-level control: no schema SELECT, only table SELECT on the tables tagged domain=pharmacy

cdr_external_researcher.description: Table-level control, narrow: approved diagnostic tables only, direct identifiers masked per the final role matrix

cdr_data_scientist.description: User-level separation: schema SELECT on silver only, direct and quasi identifiers masked. No gold access and no security administration; the full approved Silver population is the analytical surface

cdr_data_engineers.description: Platform / pipeline engineering: read, write and build across bronze, silver and gold. Unmasked where operationally required, but without catalog administration - ownership, grants and governance changes stay with cdr_admins
